why: Jayce wants to poke K'Sante out of lane with Shock Blast and hammer all-ins, but K'Sante's Footwork and Path Maker let him farm through the harass and trade back without losing the wave. Once K'Sante has resistances, Jayce's burst no longer threatens a kill, and All Out drags Jayce away from his team where his poke never fires. That durability is why K'Sante won 18 of 27 pro games (66.7%) in this pairing.
tips: Use Footwork to block Jayce's hammer knockback and keep farming instead of taking free poke trades early.
Save Path Maker to dash through the minion wave and escape when Jayce jumps in with To the Skies.
Look to use All Out near walls or toward your team so Jayce is isolated before he can poke again.

why: Rumble's Flamespitter deals sustained magic damage that K'Sante cannot itemise away with armour alone, and Scrap Shield lets Rumble trade through K'Sante's short combos. The Equalizer also zones K'Sante off waves and objective approaches, so All Out often starts from low health or bad ground. Rumble took 14 of 25 pro games (56.0%) by winning the attrition war before K'Sante could force an isolated duel.
tips: Keep your heat over 50 before trading so Flamespitter and Electro-Harpoon win extended exchanges.
Place The Equalizer across the wave or river entrance to farm safely and deny K'Sante a clean engage angle.
Hold Scrap Shield for K'Sante's knockback combo instead of spending it on poke damage.

why: Ambessa needs to chain dashes onto one target, but Mini Gnar kites her with Hyper movement speed and Boomerang poke while building rage safely at range. When Ambessa finally commits, Mega Gnar arrives with GNAR and Wallop to stun her mid-combo and win the all-in she started. Gnar won 14 of 23 pro games (60.9%) by refusing the close-range fight until Mega form flipped it.
tips: Poke with Boomerang Throw and Hop away whenever Ambessa dashes forward in Mini form.
Track your rage so you transform as Ambessa commits, then stun her against a wall with GNAR!
Avoid trading in Mini form at close range; your advantage disappears once Ambessa can stick to you.

why: Olaf wants a long lifesteal duel under Ragnarok, but Kled's Bear Trap on a Rope applies grievous wounds that cut that healing exactly when Olaf drops low. Skaarl's remount also gives Kled a second health bar, so Olaf's execute-style Reckless Swing finishes nothing and the fight turns. Kled won 12 of 20 pro games (60.0%) by shortening Olaf's sustain window and outlasting the all-in.
tips: Land Bear Trap on a Rope before Olaf gets low so grievous wounds cut his lifesteal during the all-in.
Keep fighting while dismounted to rebuild courage and remount instead of running from Olaf's chase.
Save Violent Tendencies burst for when Olaf is trapped and cannot reset the fight with Undertow axes.

why: Yorick needs Mist Walkers and the Maiden to push, but Jayce clears ghouls quickly with both forms and pokes Yorick before a cage ever traps him. Jayce's hammer knockback also answers the Dark Procession engage, and his early lane priority stops Yorick from reaching the split-push state he needs. Jayce won 12 of 19 pro games (63.2%) by killing the ghouls first and never letting Yorick play his pushing game.
tips: Clear Mist Walkers with ranged autos and Shock Blast before they reach you or your tower.
Use Thundering Blow to knock Yorick away the moment he lands Dark Procession around you.
Crash waves early and poke Yorick under tower so he cannot summon the Maiden for a free push.

why: Jax relies on Counter Strike to dodge autos and win duels, but Olaf's Reckless Swing deals true damage through it and Ragnarok ignores the stun entirely. Olaf also sustains through Jax's short trades with Vicious Strikes, so Jax never gets the clean extended duel his passive wants. Olaf won 10 of 17 pro games (58.8%) because Jax's main defensive tool simply does not work in this lane.
tips: Hold Ragnarok until Jax starts Counter Strike, then keep hitting through the stun window.
Use Reckless Swing on cooldown during Counter Strike since true damage ignores the dodge.
Pick up Undertow axes during trades to keep the slow on Jax and prevent his Leap Strike escape.

why: Mini Gnar wants to kite and poke, but Rumble's Flamespitter and Electro-Harpoon out-trade the boomerang at the same range and push the wave faster. The Equalizer punishes Gnar's Hop engages and zones Mega Gnar away from the wall slam he needs to win fights. Rumble won 10 of 16 pro games (62.5%) by winning both the Mini poke war and the Mega engage denial.
tips: Keep heat high and walk forward with Flamespitter whenever Gnar steps up for a boomerang trade.
Drop The Equalizer on Gnar's landing spot or behind him when he Hops in to force a bad transform fight.
Use double Electro-Harpoon slows to stop Mini Gnar kiting you out after a trade.

why: Rumble's damage is almost entirely magic, and Galio's Shield of Durand magic shield plus base durability absorb Flamespitter trades that would melt most top laners. Galio also clears waves with Winds of War and can follow any teleport play with Hero's Entrance, matching Rumble's map pressure. Galio won 9 of 14 pro games (64.3%) by negating Rumble's damage type and matching his roams.
tips: Trade with Winds of War and your magic shield up so Flamespitter never wins the health exchange.
Save Shield of Durand taunt for when Rumble overheats or your jungler arrives, not for poke.
Watch the map once you have Hero's Entrance and follow Rumble's first move to objectives.

why: Ambessa chains dashes to stick to a target, but Ragnarok makes Olaf immune to her knockback and slow effects while he runs her down. Olaf's true damage and sustain also win the extended melee trades Ambessa needs after her burst ends. Olaf won 8 of 14 pro games (57.1%) in this older-meta pairing.
tips: Wait for Ambessa to spend her dashes, then use Ragnarok and Ghost-style chase to stay on her.
Trade with Reckless Swing whenever she dashes in; she cannot disengage once her mobility is down.
Keep Undertow axes landing between you and Ambessa so she cannot kite out between combos.

why: Jayce should poke Rumble out, but Rumble's Scrap Shield absorbs Shock Blast poke and Flamespitter pushes the wave so Jayce cannot freeze or zone. The Equalizer also covers Jayce's hammer engage and the river approaches Jayce wants to control. Rumble won 10 of 11 pro games (90.9%), the strongest rate in this role, by shielding the poke and owning the wave.
tips: Use Scrap Shield on Jayce's Shock Blast cooldown so his poke never chips your health down.
Push with Flamespitter early to deny Jayce a freeze and force him to farm under tower.
Place The Equalizer behind Jayce when he swaps to hammer form and commits forward.

why: K'Sante wants to soak a combo and drag his opponent away with All Out, but Ambessa's repeated dashes follow him through every reposition and keep damage landing. Her Public Execution also locks K'Sante down before he can isolate a carry or escape. Ambessa won 6 of 10 pro games (60.0%) by never letting K'Sante reset the fight on his terms.
tips: Chain dashes after K'Sante uses Path Maker so he cannot create distance between trades.
Save Public Execution for when K'Sante starts All Out or tries to drag your teammate away.
Take short burst trades and dash out before K'Sante stacks his passive for a return combo.

why: Olaf's Ragnarok gives him huge resistances to survive duels, but Trundle's Subjugate steals those exact stats and turns Olaf's ultimate into Trundle's own durability. Frozen Domain also matches Olaf's chase, and Chomp trades keep Olaf from sustaining ahead. Trundle won 6 of 10 pro games (60.0%) because stealing Ragnarok's resistances flips the stat-check Olaf relies on.
tips: Cast Subjugate the moment Olaf uses Ragnarok so you steal the bonus resistances for yourself.
Fight inside Frozen Domain to match Olaf's attack speed and movement during the all-in.
Use Pillar of Ice to separate Olaf from his Undertow axes so he loses the slow reset.

why: Olaf wants to run Camille down in a straight line, but Camille's Hookshot escapes the chase and her second Precision Protocol deals true damage Olaf cannot itemise against. Hextech Ultimatum also traps Olaf away from his Undertow axes, cutting the resets his all-in needs. Camille won 6 of 10 pro games (60.0%) by leaving when Olaf commits and returning with true damage.
tips: Use Hookshot to a wall whenever Olaf uses Ragnarok instead of trading into his ultimate.
Wait for the second Precision Protocol true damage before committing to a full trade.
Trap Olaf in Hextech Ultimatum away from his dropped axes so he cannot reset Undertow.

why: K'Sante builds resistances to survive burst, but Gwen's Snip Snip deals true damage at the centre and her passive adds percent-health magic damage on every hit. Hallowed Mist also denies K'Sante clean engage angles while Gwen keeps cutting. Gwen won 6 of 9 pro games (66.7%) because true and percent-health damage ignore the tank stats K'Sante stacks.
tips: Aim the centre of Snip Snip! on K'Sante to land the true damage portion every trade.
Stand inside Hallowed Mist during fights so K'Sante cannot target you cleanly from outside it.
Stack your passive with autos and Needlework between snips to keep percent-health damage flowing.

why: Ambessa out-dashes most fighters, but Camille's Hookshot matches her mobility and Tactical Sweep slows her re-engage. Hextech Ultimatum then locks Ambessa in place where Precision Protocol true damage wins the duel she cannot kite. Camille won 5 of 9 pro games (55.6%) in a close pairing decided by who controls the engage distance.
tips: Use Tactical Sweep while Ambessa dashes in to slow her and win the short trade.
Save Hookshot to follow Ambessa's escape dash or to leave before her full combo lands.
Only use Hextech Ultimatum when your second Precision Protocol is ready for the true damage hit.

why: Renekton wants early Slice and Dice all-ins, but Mini Gnar pokes him down with Boomerang Throw before he can reach the wave. When Renekton finally dashes in, Mega Gnar's stuns and percent-health damage win the extended fight Renekton falls off from. Gnar won 5 of 9 pro games (55.6%) by surviving the early power spike and scaling past it.
tips: Poke Renekton with Boomerang Throw whenever he walks up to build fury on the wave.
Hop backward as Renekton uses Slice and Dice so his second dash cannot reach you.
Time Mega form for Renekton's all-in and stun him into a wall before trading back.

why: Gnar controls lane with Mini range, but Twisted Fate matches the poke with Wild Cards and Pick a Card gold card stops Gnar's Hop engage cold. Destiny also lets Twisted Fate follow Gnar's teleport plays or punish his split-push with a numbers advantage. Twisted Fate won 5 of 9 pro games (55.6%) in this flex pairing by denying Gnar's engage timing.
tips: Lock a gold card whenever Gnar Hops forward or starts building rage near your team.
Clear waves with Red Card and Wild Cards to match Gnar's push before roaming with Destiny.
Use Destiny to punish Gnar while he is in Mini form and cannot win a forced fight.

why: Aatrox needs to land sweet-spot Q hits to heal and win trades, but Ambessa dashes through the Q zones and stays inside the range where Aatrox deals least. Her mobility also dodges Infernal Chains, so Aatrox never locks her down for a full combo. Ambessa won 5 of 9 pro games (55.6%) in this older-meta pairing.
tips: Dash inside Aatrox's Q sweet spots so his hits deal reduced damage and miss the knock-up.
Save a dash to exit whenever Aatrox lands Infernal Chains instead of fighting in the pull zone.
Take short combos between Aatrox Q cooldowns rather than standing in his World Ender all-in.

why: Vayne top relies on Tumble kiting and Condemn to keep fighters away, but Ragnarok makes Olaf immune to Condemn and slows while he closes the gap. Once Olaf reaches her, Vayne's low base health cannot survive Reckless Swing true damage and Undertow resets. Olaf won 7 of 8 pro games (87.5%) because Vayne's only peel tools stop working the moment Olaf ults.
tips: Do not use Ragnarok until Vayne has shown Tumble or is positioned for a Condemn attempt.
Throw Undertow through Vayne's Tumble path and pick up the axe to keep the chase going.
Trade aggressively before Vayne completes her first item; she cannot duel you early.

why: Jayce pokes and knocks Olaf back with Thundering Blow, but Ragnarok ignores the knockback and slow effects so one committed chase reaches him. Olaf's sustain then wins the melee trade Jayce's hammer form cannot finish. Olaf won 5 of 8 pro games (62.5%) in this older-meta pairing.
tips: Hold Ragnarok for Jayce's hammer form engage so his knockback cannot save him.
Run through Shock Blast poke without stopping; your sustain recovers the chip damage.
Keep Undertow landing behind Jayce to cut off his Acceleration Gate escape.

why: Mini Gnar kites with slows and Hop, but Ragnarok removes those slows and lets Olaf run straight onto him. Mega Gnar's stuns also fail against Ragnarok, so Gnar has no form that stops the chase. Olaf won 4 of 7 pro games (57.1%) by removing Gnar's kiting tools in both forms.
tips: Use Ragnarok as Gnar transforms or Hops so neither his stuns nor slows can stop you.
Chase Mini Gnar before rage fills; he cannot fight back without Mega stats.
Pick up Undertow axes along the chase path to keep pressure between Reckless Swings.

why: Gnar wants to poke and kite in Mini form, but K'Sante's durability lets him farm through boomerang harass and contest the wave. All Out then removes Mega Gnar from his team context and forces a duel K'Sante's resistances win. K'Sante won 4 of 7 pro games (57.1%) in this older-meta pairing.
tips: Farm through Mini Gnar poke with Footwork instead of chasing trades you cannot reach.
Use All Out on Mega Gnar toward your team so his GNAR! cannot hit multiple teammates.
Save Path Maker to reposition when Gnar Hops in with rage nearly full.

why: Zaahen stacks Determination in extended fights and revives when filled, so trades must end fast or not happen. Ambessa's dash chains let her take short burst trades and leave before Determination fills, denying the revive value entirely. Ambessa won all 6 pro games (100%), though the sample is small, by refusing the long duel Zaahen needs.
tips: Take one dash-in combo and dash out before Zaahen stacks Determination from hitting you.
Save Public Execution for after Zaahen's revive is spent or when he cannot trigger it.
Do not stand in Zaahen's ultimate rise; dash out and re-engage once its damage reduction ends.

why: Zaahen needs time to stack Determination and wants to revive through burst, but Olaf's sustained true damage keeps dealing through the revive health pool. Ragnarok also ignores Zaahen's knock-up and pull, so Olaf never loses the chase. Olaf won all 6 pro games (100%) in this older-meta pairing, on a small sample.
tips: Keep auto-attacking through Zaahen's revive instead of backing off when he falls.
Use Ragnarok to ignore Zaahen's knock-up combo and stay in melee range.
Use Reckless Swing on cooldown; true damage cuts the revived health pool fastest.

why: Jayce should poke Sion out of lane, but Sion's Soul Furnace shield and base health absorb Shock Blast harass while Decimating Smash clears waves Jayce wants to freeze. Sion also scales into a front line Jayce cannot kill, and Unstoppable Onslaught threatens Jayce's immobile poke stance in fights. Sion won 5 of 6 pro games (83.3%) by surviving the lane Jayce must win early.
tips: Use Soul Furnace shield as Jayce fires Shock Blast so his poke trades into your shield.
Clear the wave with Decimating Smash and Roar of the Slayer instead of chasing Jayce for trades.
Once you have health and armour, walk at Jayce to deny him free poke angles on your team.

why: Tristana top matches Mini Gnar's range, out-pushes him with Explosive Charge, and Rocket Jump resets let her follow or escape Hop plays. Buster Shot also knocks Mega Gnar out of his engage before GNAR lands. Tristana won 5 of 6 pro games (83.3%) in this older-meta flex pairing, on a small sample.
tips: Stack Explosive Charge on Gnar or the wave to win push and force him to farm under tower.
Save Rocket Jump until Gnar uses Hop so you can follow his escape or leave his engage.
Hold Buster Shot for Mega Gnar's leap so his GNAR! never connects with your team.

why: Mini Gnar kites most melee champions, but Jax's Leap Strike closes the gap and Counter Strike dodges boomerang autos while the stun sets up his burst. Jax also scales harder, so Gnar's window closes once Jax completes his first items. Jax won 4 of 6 pro games (66.7%) by reaching Mini Gnar and winning the scaling race.
tips: Leap Strike onto Mini Gnar right after he throws Boomerang so he cannot kite the trade.
Activate Counter Strike as you land to dodge his autos and stun him for your burst.
Do not leap into Mega Gnar near a wall; wait for Mini form before committing.

why: Mundo scales into an unkillable tank, but Renekton's empowered Ruthless Predator and early damage threaten kills before Mundo's health stacking comes online. Renekton's lane priority also denies Mundo free farm and forces him to spend health answering the pressure. Renekton won 4 of 6 pro games (66.7%) by ending the lane before Mundo's scaling starts.
tips: Build 50 fury before trading so empowered Ruthless Predator wins the exchange decisively.
Use Slice and Dice through the wave to reach Mundo, then dice out before he returns damage.
Force trades whenever Mundo walks up for a cleaver last-hit in the early levels.

why: Ambessa's damage comes from dashing in and auto-attacking between abilities, but Counter Strike dodges those autos and stuns her mid-chain. Leap Strike also follows her escape dash, so Ambessa cannot choose when the duel ends. Jax won 4 of 6 pro games (66.7%) in this older-meta pairing.
tips: Start Counter Strike as Ambessa dashes in so her combo autos miss and she takes the stun.
Save Leap Strike to follow Ambessa's escape dash instead of opening with it.
Take longer trades once Counter Strike ends; your passive attack speed wins extended duels.
